questions.element: /frontier at 390 — the board (3 columns x 16 rows); every other captured route passes at both widths
questions.note: The 390 capture is a 928px-wide document (dark identical), so the board's two index columns sit off-frame and the flagship's primary content needs horizontal scroll; home, catalog, wiki index/entry/model, tools, learn, blog, tutorials, routine, data and colophon all state purpose and lead content in the first viewport at both widths.

questions.element: / — the EVERYTHING HERE side list's last row (The Frontier); the header nav
questions.note: The feed half is met — WHAT CHANGED leads with no hero and the door displaces nothing — but the door is the last row of the side list, near y1310 against a 900px fold at 1440 and some three viewports down at 390 (home--dark--390.png), and /frontier is absent from the nav, so the flagship has no first-viewport door.

F-K12 is built as written — at 390 the order is title, alias line, one lede paragraph, then FACTS, and at 1440 the lede opens the left column with FACTS starting lower in the right (wiki-entry--light--1440.png) — and the prose-less model record reads coherently facts-first (wiki-model--light--1440.png), closing F-hier-3.

Every index lands the eye on its discriminating value first — record name on /wiki with type and status in muted mono, listing name on /tools, page title on /learn, headline on /blog and /tutorials, pair title on /impossible-routine, model name on /catalog — dates and repeated verification stamps held behind them.

questions.element: /frontier board (class rules REQUIRED, absent); /catalog@390 provider-group summaries (class rules FORBIDDEN, present)
questions.note: Classes assigned: REQUIRED on the catalog table, the home changed feed, /tools listings and the /frontier board (16 rows x 3 columns across ~1150px is R8's cross-row drift case), FORBIDDEN on /wiki, /data, /learn, /blog, /tutorials and the closed /catalog@390 provider list; the board carries only a header and a closing rule where R8 requires per-row ones, and the provider list rules between every pair of uniform single-line disclosure rows where R8 forbids it (table-catalog--light--390.png).

Catalog@390 is the round's biggest density win — 93,963px of flat stack in round 0 against 3,041px of counted provider groups now — but /frontier does not hold: 3,546px at 1440 against a 928px-wide 6,453px document at 390, so content per screen falls instead of reflowing; the wiki entry still leaves its right track near-empty below FACTS at 1440 (declared S18 debt, not re-filed).

The desktop table's row ruling did not disappear at 390, it moved — some 45 hairlines now divide a uniform list of disclosure controls that each already carry a name and a count, a channel change rather than a removal — and a smaller instance sits under the /impossible-routine pair title, where a short rule and a full-width rule stack with an empty band between (routine--light--1440.png).

Judged only from the declared class — PNGs at 1440 and 390 in both themes plus the round-0 set for before/after — with no hover, focus, motion or scroll state claimed and nothing inferred below a fold; the /frontier 390 overflow is read from the capture's own rendered document width, which the rig demonstrably reports (tutorial--390 is 473px wide this round, 462px in round 0), not from a DOM measurement.

findings.problem: The new flagship does not reflow: /frontier renders a 928px document at a 390 viewport, so the board's two index columns and every value in them fall outside the frame.
findings.invariant: At a 390 viewport /frontier's rendered document width equals 390px and the board's own columns are reachable without horizontal scroll.
findings.prescription: Fold the board below the template's narrow breakpoint the way /catalog@390 already folds — one organisation per stacked record with its index cells beneath the name.

findings.problem: The Frontier's door on home is the last row of a nine-row side list and the route is absent from the nav, so the flagship is invisible from the home first viewport at both widths.
findings.invariant: A link to /frontier is visible in the home first viewport at 1440 and at 390.
findings.prescription: Promote the door above the side list, or add /frontier to the primary nav beside catalog.

findings.problem: All 32 board cells carry the identical sentence 'no index published for this window', so the flagship's first viewport at 1440 is a grid of one repeated string with no discriminating value in it.
findings.invariant: A column with nothing published states its absence once, at the column, not once per row.
findings.prescription: Collapse a wholly-empty column to its header plus one line and leave its cells blank, which is both the packet's declared empty_state and K21's own blank-cell reading.

findings.problem: The board is R8's rules-required shape — 16 rows by 3 columns across some 1150px — but carries only a header and a closing rule, so a value will drift from its organisation once the cells hold real numbers.
findings.invariant: The board's sibling rows carry a rule between every pair, or the surface is justified against R8's own test rather than by analogy to a link index.
findings.prescription: Rule the board's rows as the catalog table's rows are ruled.

findings.problem: Catalog@390's closed provider list carries a hairline between every pair of near-uniform single-line disclosure rows, the chrome R8 forbids on that class, and it is where the desktop table's ruling relocated to.
findings.invariant: In its closed state the provider list carries no rule between every pair; a boundary appears only around a group that is open.
findings.prescription: Drop the closed-state rule and draw the group boundary on the open state only.

findings.problem: On the /tutorials index each listing's meta line paints its date and the word 'verified' on top of each other, leaving the row's provenance illegible; present in the round-0 capture too, so carried debt rather than a regression.
findings.invariant: No two text runs in a /tutorials listing meta line share the same line box at 1440 or 390.
findings.prescription: Give the meta line its own row in the listing grid instead of overlaying the two runs.

carried_forward: F-hier-1 (site-wide spine with no per-surface R8 class) — declined with cause and resolved in the build: the spine was not carried onto /wiki, /data, /tools, /blog, /tutorials or /learn, which stay unruled link indexes; not re-filed.

F-hier-2 (the cadence argument rode on an aria-hidden decorative track) — resolved: THE PACE carries a digit-free prose legend saying a longer gap on the page is a longer gap in the world (frontier--light--1440.png).
F-hier-3 (element order unstated for model records) — resolved: /wiki/model renders title, status, FACTS with nothing to precede them (wiki-model--light--1440.png).

F-hier-4 (time-proportional gaps pushing home feed items below the 390 fold) — did not manifest: home's feed rows are evenly spaced and the page grew 86px against round 0 (home--dark--390.png); the proportional spine is confined to /frontier.

diagnosis.strongest: HIER on the surfaces the packet actually reworked — F-K12 lands cleanly at both widths, every index still leads with its discriminating value, and /frontier's prose legend and per-cell empty states say what each region is before any number appears.
diagnosis.weakest: DENS on the new flagship — /frontier is at once the widest surface on the site and the only one that does not reflow, and its board spends a full desktop viewport on 32 copies of one sentence.
diagnosis.critical_issue: /frontier renders a 928px document at a 390 viewport, so the board K19 requires it to lead with is horizontally clipped and its index columns are off-frame at the width most readers arrive on.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Fold the /frontier board below the narrow breakpoint into stacked per-organisation records the way /catalog@390 now folds — it settles the critical question and reuses a mechanism this build already proved.

downstream.weakness: The concept round's chrome risk moved rather than closed: the spine was correctly withheld from the link indexes, but the surface it was built for carries the site's only unreflowed layout, and the catalog's ruling reappeared on a uniform list at 390.
downstream.cause: Every 390 decision in this build was made on templates the rig had captured before; /frontier is new, so its narrow state was never compared against a prior capture and the packet's own reflow fence was never read back off a picture.
downstream.recommendation: Treat the 390 capture of any new route as a gate rather than a judgement — a fullPage capture wider than its viewport is a build failure, and it costs nothing to check before a panel is paid for.
